## Role in the Rating Process

The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) publishes the euro-area AAA yield curve that determines the Safe Rate (C4). It provides inflation projections used for the [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd) (C2). The bank reports government bond yields and spreads, which feed into the [Haircut](../parameters/haircut.qmd) calculation (R4). Together with the [European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd), the [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) acts as a backstop provider (R6). Holdings of government bonds by the Eurosystem are a key factor in determining the market-held portion of the debt, affecting the [Refinancing Need](../parameters/refinancing-need.qmd) assessment (R1-A*).

## Evidence by Country

### Euro Area

- The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) provides the broader macroeconomic context and euro-area inflation averages against which country-specific inflation is compared. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) provides the euro-area inflation average used for comparison. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)’s composite indicator of systemic sovereign stress (SovCISS) is used to monitor short-term sovereign risk. The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)’s policy rates and asset purchase programs are noted in the context of financing conditions and debt holder composition. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 21, 23, 74" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 21, 23, 74">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) participates in the Debt Sustainability Analysis working group. Its composite indicator of systemic sovereign stress (SovCISS) is referenced in market risk charts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) is expected to cautiously tighten its monetary policy stance, with markets pricing in policy rates of around 2.6% in the first quarter of 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 37">ⓘ</button>

### [Germany](../countries/germany.qmd)

- The European Central Bank started to ease monetary policy in 2024, reducing policy rates from 4% in June 2024 to 2.25% in April 2025. ### [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd)

- The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) provided input for the 2025 EU-wide stress test conducted by the European Banking Authority, which confirmed the resilience of Greek banks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 64-65" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 64-65">ⓘ</button>
- Greece’s credit rating returned to investment grade in late 2023, making Greek sovereign bonds eligible for the [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)’s monetary policy operations in the standard collateral framework.
